reference.title: Cable Standing Fly
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read and the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the arms open, breathe out as you hug them back together.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s opening, short stretch, about 1.5 s closing

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can sweep through the full arc with the elbow bend unchanged.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on each stack; slower opening

cues.text: Stand between two towers with the pulleys a little above shoulder height, one D-handle in each hand, feet hip width, a slight forward lean; hands together in front of the chest, elbows softly bent.
Breathe in and let the cables draw the arms open in a wide arc, elbow bend fixed, chest up.
Stop with the hands about in line with the shoulders and a stretch across the chest, not in the front of the shoulder.
Breathe out and hug the handles back together along the same arc, as if around a big tree.
Squeeze the chest with the handles just apart in front of the breastbone; keep the shoulders down.

mistakes.mistake: Turning the fly into a press
mistakes.fix: Keep the same soft elbow bend all the way out and back.

mistakes.mistake: Opening too far behind the body
mistakes.fix: Stop with the hands about in line with the shoulders.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging or rolling the shoulders forward
mistakes.fix: Shoulders down and back, chest up; lighten the stacks.

mistakes.mistake: Rocking the trunk to swing the handles
mistakes.fix: Brace, keep the lean fixed and move only at the shoulders.

kinematics.norm: Fixed soft bend of about 20-30 degrees, as in the dumbbell fly protocol of Solstad 2020
From hands together in front of the chest to about in line with the shoulders (clinical opinion)
Neutral: palms facing each other in front, forward when open (clinical opinion)
One cable per hand from its own pulley a little above shoulder height (clinical opinion)
Slight forward lean, braced and still (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s out and 1.5 s back (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Standing Fly, video (movement reference)

Solstad, Andersen, Shaw, Hoel, Vonheim and Saeterbakken 2020, a comparison of muscle activation between barbell bench press and dumbbell flyes in resistance-trained males (J Sports Sci Med 19(4):645-651; PMC7675616)
Welsch, Bird and Mayhew 2005, electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid muscles during three upper-body lifts (J Strength Cond Res 19(2):449-452)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control through the whole arc without the elbows bending more.
Do not let the cables pull the arms far behind the body: the stretched shoulder is the vulnerable position (clinical opinion).
Take the handles one at a time and step forward into position; return them the same way rather than letting the stacks drop.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: shorten the arc so the hands stop in front of the shoulders.
Balance: use a staggered stance with one foot forward.
progressions: Slower opening with a 1 s pause in the stretch.
Cable low fly or decline fly for a different line of pull.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Prime mover: draws the arm across the body (horizontal adduction). Flyes and the bench press activated the pectoralis similarly in trained men (Solstad 2020); the cable keeps tension even with the hands together.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Prime mover: draws the arm across the body (horizontal adduction). Flyes and the bench press activated the pectoralis similarly in trained men (Solstad 2020); the cable keeps tension even with the hands together.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Holds the soft elbow bend against the cable.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Holds the soft elbow bend against the cable.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Steadies the shoulder blade on the ribcage.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Steadies the shoulder blade on the ribcage.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Keeps the elbow from bending further.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Keeps the elbow from bending further.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Centres the head of the humerus in the stretch.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Centres the head of the humerus in the stretch.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the slight lean still against the pull of both cables.
